newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar shunted in volatile range, downside seen.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar shunted in volatile range, downside seen.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended lower on Wednesday after being shunted around in a volatile range. Dealers expect to see further downside.
Kiwi ended at US$0.6946/53 and at 66.26 on the Trade Weighted Index from 0.6985/92, 66.38 at the open.
One dealer said he had seen strong overseas selling pressure throughout the session, partly offset by exporter buying. "But really all we've seen is sellers," he said.
In the end, the currency was little changed after the official signing of Tuesday's coalition deal, which laid out more detail on what form the legislative programme would take.
"But we see a weaker currency and profit taking," he said. "The window has closed from a samurai and euro issuance point of view," he said.
A string of dual currency issuance has been a key factor in the Kiwi's rally over recent months.
Next on the agenda was Tuesday's monetary policy statement, but dealers do not expect to see a further easing, despite the change in the political structure and evidence the economy may be slowing.
"Personally, I don't think we'll see one because the market has eased already," he said.
From here dealers expected to see controlled profit-taking after the currency's meteoric rise.
Another dealer said the currency was shunted around in a relatively tight 0.6950-95 range but the movements within that were volatile.
"It looks like it's going to go lower," he said, adding there appeared interest to buy at 0.6950. "The market has got to be careful not to get too short.
"With these comments coming from politicians the risk is still lower," he said.

New Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters, who is also to take up the new role of Treasurer, earlier said exporters would now take a positive view of the currency, which had fallen about a U.S. cent since just before the coalition announcement on Tuesday eventing.
